scope: Narrow new Windows drive-spelling reconciliation, existing shared root identity check, actual recovery flush and new spelling tests; not a new full audit of all transplanted provider files.
conclusion: No new blocking defect found in the reviewed narrow changes. Current exact-head hosted native qualification remains required.
confirmed: same_recovery_home only reconciles Disk/VerbatimDisk with matching drive and remaining Path components. Other namespaces and directories reject; non-Windows retains direct path equality.
bind_existing_recovery_database, guard revalidate_for, and materialize target-parent checks all use the same comparison; retained handles continue their existing identity and permission validation.

Removing the duplicate Memory canonical_root != root check does not remove canonical_path_without_redirection: Unix equality remains there, and Windows shared validation still checks component equivalence and every ancestor for a reparse attribute. Local NTFS restriction remains a separate retained-provider gate.

Candidate synchronization opens a writable Windows file and propagates sync_all failure. Directory synchronization obtains the existing private directory for sync and performs a real sync_all; opening a handle alone is not acknowledged as durability.

materialize copy keeps fixed per-object and aggregate size limits, validates retained source before and after reading, uses create-new private child creation, never copies SHM, and propagates file/directory flush errors.

New state tests cover both spellings, different-root/namespace denial, no outside target creation and unchanged source bytes. New Memory test uses exact-current-cut witness and original authority verifier for both actual root spellings.
limits: Static read-only review only: no Rust compilation, native Windows execution, SQLite recovery or test controls were run here.
No reuse of old e9cf provider PASS as qualification for this new combined commit.
Point-in-time absent-sidecar checks do not establish an atomic absence lease; this review does not expand the original recovery contract.
No change to global scientific or production HOLD status.
